SECR Package
Spatially Explicit Capture Recapture
Estimate the density and size of spatially distributed animal populations from detector arrays via passive acoustic monitors (PAMs), using maximum-likelihood SECR models. Tools are included for data manipulation and model selection. SECR models the locations of detections and the histories of marked animals, allowing you to estimate population density and to fit a model to show how probability declines with distance from each detector, including spatial/temporal trends.
Detection functions describe how the probability of being detected a a given detector declines with distance from animals activity centre, most commonly used is HalfNormal (HN).






Note



The secr R package assumes the population is closed during the sampling period so no animals move out of the area - no births, deaths, immigration or emigration occurs ().



1 First install from CRAN: install.packages(“secr”)
2 Load package: library(secr)
3 List all available detection functions: ?detectfn

text:
SECR Package
Spatially Explicit Capture Recapture






Note



To access the function, first install SECR, install.packages(“secr”)


Functions to estimate the density and size of a spatially distributed animal population sampled with an array of passive acoustic monitors (PAMs). Models incorporate distance-dependent detection to maximise the likelihood. Tools are included for data manipulation and model selection. Spatially explicit capture-recapture is a set of methods for studying marked animals distributed in space. Data consists from the location of detectors and their histories of marked animals. Models for population density and detection are defined in secr. Density models may include spatial/temporal trends, with predictors corresponding to time or behaviour.
